title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey, December 2026 — the pre-cliff snapshot published on day 4 of a possible lapse, 8:30 a.m. ET
source: EST: newyorkfed.org/survey/empire/empiresurvey_overview — the New York Fed's own Empire State Manufacturing Survey overview page, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,467 bytes) by this event's own never-assessed initial research, independently of the empire-state-mfg-2026-09-15 sweep that proposed this entry. Its 2026 release grid enumerates the full year verbatim — JAN 15 · FEB 17 · MAR 16 · APR 15 · MAY 15 · JUN 15 · JUL 15 · AUG 17 · SEP 15 · OCT 15 · NOV 16 · DEC 15 — above the page's own timing note 'Released at or shortly after 8:30 a.m.' Independently reproduced by the survey's published rule (the 15th of the month, rolled forward off weekends: Feb 15 2026 was a Sunday and the grid shows Feb 17, Aug 15 was a Saturday and the grid shows Aug 17); 2026-12-15 is a Tuesday, so no roll applies. Filed estimate on the two standing counts every sibling regional-survey entry documents, neither of which is doubt about the date: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane does not self-confirm. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/empire-state-mfg-2026-12-15.from-empire-state-mfg-2026-09-15.json) and re-verified its primary independently, as the proposal asked the canonical author to do. The proposal's coverage argument — that this is the calendar's earliest post-cliff Fed-funded manufacturing read — is HALF CORRECTED here, and the correction is the entry's reason to exist. Initial research (docs/research/events/empire-state-mfg-2026-12-15.md) measured three things the proposal could not. FIRST, the collection rule is PUBLISHED, not inferred: the same overview page states the survey 'is sent on the first day of each month to the same pool of about 200 manufacturing executives... Most are completed by the tenth, although surveys are accepted until the fifteenth.' December's bulk window therefore closes 2026-12-10, ONE DAY BEFORE the 12-11 cliff, and the acceptance tail (12-11 to 12-15) is truncated by the release itself. The December print is a PRE-cliff snapshot published on day 4 of a possible lapse — not the first post-cliff read. The first regional survey whose bulk window would sit inside a lapse is Empire's JANUARY 2027 edition (collection Jan 1-10), and a 2018-19-length 35-day lapse from 2026-12-12 runs to about 2027-01-16, which covers exactly that window. SECOND, a lapse leaves no measurable mark on this survey anyway. In the four months of Empire's 302 whose collection window sat inside a federal funding lapse — 2013-10 (Oct 1-17 lapse), 2019-01 (Dec 22-Jan 25), and 2025-10 and 2025-11 (the 43-day 2025-10-01 to 2025-11-12 lapse) — the headline changed -3.9, -1.0, +14.8 and +5.7, the 29.6th, 8.6th, 84.4th and 42.9th percentiles of absolute monthly change, two up and two down. THIRD, the FRED pull runs 302 unbroken months 2001-07 to 2026-08 with ZERO missing months across every one of those lapses, which is the empirical grounding for the proposal's Fed-funding claim and for the only thing the 12-15 morning reliably offers: on the branch where ppi-2026-12-15 (medium, confirmed BLS:, and slipped 40 days in the 2025 lapse) does not print, Empire's prices-paid index has the 8:30 slot alone and is the best available stand-in for the missing number — R-squared 0.388 against November PPI final-demand m/m (n=200, t=11.22) against 0.174 for PPI's own prior reading, which it subsumes (joint R-squared 0.391). In the units anyone would act on that is a 22 percent uncertainty cut, residual sd 0.284pp on an unconditional 0.362pp, degrading to roughly 10 percent post-2021 (RMSE 0.326pp) — best available and still not usable. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the same grounds as every sibling regional-survey entry: a single-state qualitative diffusion index over roughly 100 respondents, no house playbook keyed to regional surveys, and no tracked name carrying a New York district manufacturing channel. This entry is an ESTIMATE, which widens caution and licenses nothing.
